subject: Meteorology
title: Tropical vs. Midlatitude Weather
description: A quick, practical guide to Tropical vs. Midlatitude Weather.

hook.text: Tropical weather runs on different rules than midlatitude weather—temperature contrasts barely matter here.

buildup.text: In midlatitudes, fronts and temperature gradients drive weather; in the tropics, moisture and convection dominate.

discovery.text: The Coriolis effect is weak near the equator, so large-scale low-pressure systems can't spin up easily.

twist.text: Tropical forecasting relies more on satellite imagery and moisture fields than on pressure maps from higher latitudes.

climax.text: Diurnal cycles dominate—ocean thunderstorms peak at dawn, land storms peak in the afternoon, every single day.

punchline.text: Same atmosphere, different rulebook—the tropics play their own game.

quiz.question: What drives tropical weather more than midlatitude weather?
